title: issue2pr manifest-mode input
description: The input contract for manifest mode: everything a programmatic dispatcher supplies in place of a work-item id and the prompts a normal run would ask. This is NOT the run manifest — that one is keyed `schema_version` and handled by scripts/profile_manifest.py. The two share a word and nothing else. Three constraints from the source deliberately do not appear here: `const` values pinning a repository id and a base branch, which are project values a project-neutral contract cannot carry, and a cap on `repos`, which would contradict the core's recorded property that it never assumes arity. The first two are checked at the entry path, which knows the bound profile; a schema does not. The `$id` is relative rather than an absolute URL under a repository: an absolute one would name a project, and the guard that checks this file for project values catches it — which is what putting the schema inside CORE_FILES is for.

manifest_version.description: The input contract's version. Distinct from the run manifest's `schema_version`.

slug.description: The work-branch slug, under the slug rule the issue2pr profile contract declares (profile-contract.md <!-- slug-rule -->): lower-case ASCII letters, digits and '-', at most 40 characters, never '-'-led; the lookahead is end-of-input (a '$' would admit a trailing newline under re.search). A supplied slug outside it is refused here, before anything is created.

body_path.description: Path to the brief this subtask's body lives in. Required, which is why a shipped example is a brief and a manifest rather than a manifest alone.

repos.description: No `maxItems`. The source pinned this at 1; skills/issue2pr/references/boundary-inventory.md records one-repository-per-run as an assumption resolved by `repo_path accepts a list; core never assumes arity`. Porting the cap would ship a schema contradicting the core it serves.

id.description: No `const`. The source pinned a repository name, which is a project value. Whether this id matches the bound profile is checked at the entry path, which has a profile to compare against.

base_branch.description: No `const`, for the same reason as `id`, and checked in the same place.

max_review_iterations.description: The source spelling, kept deliberately. The core's run state and CLI say `max_review_rounds`; translation happens at the entry path, because renaming a specified input property would be a fourth port-time correction this contract does not authorise.
